section: Anti-caste and non-Brahmin movements - Jyotiba Phule and Satyashodhak Samaj, Narayana Guru, Periyar, Justice Party
subsections: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact
South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim
Andhra leaders of the party - office held
Relations with Congress and the Swaraj Party

accepted.s: Which organisation was established by B.R. Ambedkar in 1924 for the welfare of the excluded sections?
accepted.x: Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was established in 1924 by B.R. Ambedkar for the welfare and advancement of the excluded sections.
accepted.tq: Use the direct year–organisation association.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following events associated with B.R. Ambedkar:
1. Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
2. Mahad Satyagraha
3. Kalaram Temple Satyagraha
4. Conversion to Buddhism
Which of the following is the correct chronological order?
accepted.x: The events occurred in 1924, 1927, 1930 and 1956 respectively.
accepted.tq: Arrange the events by identifying their years first.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: On which date was Manusmriti Dahan associated with Ambedkar’s Mahad movement observed?
accepted.x: Manusmriti Dahan was observed on 25 December 1927 during the period of the Mahad Satyagraha.
accepted.tq: Test the exact date attached to a major reform event.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha associated with B.R. Ambedkar took place in:
accepted.x: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha took place in 1930.
accepted.tq: Distinguish between closely spaced movement years.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936. The Scheduled Castes Federation was formed in 1942, while the conversion took place in 1956.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year–organisation pair and eliminate the shifted dates.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In the 1937 Bombay Assembly elections, how many candidates of the Independent Labour Party, including Ambedkar, won?
accepted.x: Ambedkar and 15 other candidates of the Independent Labour Party won, making the total 16 successful candidates.
accepted.tq: Read the numerical statement precisely by distinguishing the leader from the total.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following journals was NOT associated with B.R. Ambedkar?
accepted.x: Mooknayak, Bahishkrit Bharat and Janata were associated with Ambedkar. Justice was the English newspaper of the Justice Party.
accepted.tq: Find the odd newspaper from the neighbouring organisational group.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The expression “Mooknayak” literally means:
accepted.x: Mooknayak means “Leader of the Silent”.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a distinctive journal title.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Poona Pact:
1. It was signed on 24 September 1932.
2. It replaced separate electorates with reserved seats in joint electorates.
3. It provided 148 seats in place of the 71 seats under the Communal Award.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 and altered the arrangement of representation from separate electorates to reserved seats in joint electorates, with 148 seats instead of 71.
accepted.tq: Verify the date, constitutional arrangement and numerical comparison separately.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: B.R. Ambedkar agreed to the Poona Pact reluctantly primarily because he wished to:
o: obtain a separate province for Dalits
secure the survival of the Justice Party
accepted.x: Ambedkar accepted the change from separate electorates to reserved seats in joint electorates reluctantly in order to save Gandhi’s life.
accepted.tq: Link the political compromise with the immediate circumstance behind it.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The mass conversion to Buddhism led by B.R. Ambedkar took place at Deeksha Bhoomi, Nagpur, on:
accepted.x: The mass conversion took place at Deeksha Bhoomi, Nagpur, on 14 October 1956 and was associated with 22 vows.
accepted.tq: Combine place, date and event rather than relying on the year alone.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: How many vows were associated with Ambedkar’s mass conversion to Neo-Buddhism?
accepted.x: The mass conversion to Buddhism at Nagpur was accompanied by 22 vows.
accepted.tq: Test the exact numerical detail attached to a recognised event.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following titles was NOT associated with B.R. Ambedkar?
accepted.x: Messenger of Dalits, Modern Manu and Baba Saheb were titles associated with Ambedkar. Panagal Raja was a Justice Party leader.
accepted.tq: Reject the title belonging to a different political personality.
accepted.sec: Ambedkar - satyagrahas, journals, honorary degrees, Neo-Buddhism, Poona Pact  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The South Indian People's Association was formed at Victoria Memorial Hall, Madras, on:
accepted.x: Around 30 non-Brahmin leaders met at Victoria Memorial Hall, Madras, on 20 November 1916 and formed the South Indian People's Association.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the association’s founding date from the later newspaper date.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The political wing of the South Indian People's Association was known as the:
accepted.x: The South Indian Liberal Federation was the political wing of the South Indian People's Association and later became popularly known as the Justice Party.
accepted.tq: Test the relationship between a parent association and its political wing.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who signed the Non-Brahmin Manifesto of December 1916?
accepted.x: The Non-Brahmin Manifesto issued in December 1916 was signed by P. Thyagaraya Chetty.
accepted.tq: Use the signatory–document association rather than the founder list.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The English daily Justice, which gave its name to the South Indian Liberal Federation, was launched on:
accepted.x: The English daily Justice was launched on 26 February 1917, after which the South Indian Liberal Federation became popularly known as the Justice Party.
accepted.tq: Separate the formation date from the newspaper-launch date.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the founders of the South Indian Liberal Federation?
accepted.x: C. Natesa Mudaliar, T.M. Nair and P. Thyagaraya Chetty were founders of the South Indian Liberal Federation. C.R. Das was associated with the Swaraj Party.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider from a nearby political organisation.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What was the symbol of the Justice Party?
accepted.x: The symbol of the Justice Party was the Scales.
accepted.tq: Test a distinctive organisational symbol directly.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The first general meeting of the South Indian Liberal Federation was held at Coimbatore on:
accepted.x: The first general meeting was held at Coimbatore on 19 July 1917, with Panagal Raja presiding.
accepted.tq: Match the meeting with its place, date and presiding leader.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The principal aim of the Justice Party was to:
o: organise the armed struggle against British rule
secure separate electorates for Muslims בלבד
accepted.x: The Justice Party was established primarily to protect the interests of non-Brahmins in the Madras Presidency.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated institutional aim without being distracted by broader movements.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the social base of the Justice Party:
1. Its base included non-Brahmin landed gentry.
2. In Andhra, Reddys, Kammas and Kapus formed part of this social base.
3. Brahmins constituted approximately 90 per cent of the Presidency’s population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Brahmins were approximately 3 per cent of the Presidency’s population, not 90 per cent; the 90 per cent-plus figure referred to their share of government jobs.
accepted.tq: Catch the reversed population-versus-employment comparison.
accepted.sec: South Indian Liberal Federation - founding and aim  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In the Madras Presidency election of 1920, the Justice Party secured:
accepted.x: In the 1920 election, held after the Congress boycott, the Justice Party won 63 of the 98 seats and formed the first ministry.
accepted.tq: Match the election year with its exact seat result.
accepted.sec: Elections and ministries under dyarchy  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Justice Party’s result in 1926 and the position of other groups?
accepted.x: In 1926, the Justice Party won 22 seats, while the Swaraj Party won 41 and independents won 36.
accepted.tq: Compare all three figures in the same election rather than recalling one number in isolation.
accepted.sec: Elections and ministries under dyarchy  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First Justice Party ministry
B. Election in which the Justice Party won 44 seats
C. Election in which the Justice Party won 22 seats
D. Congress ministry under Rajaji
accepted.x: The sequence is 1920 election and first ministry, 1923 election with 44 seats, 1926 election with 22 seats, and 1937 Congress ministry under Rajaji.
accepted.tq: Use the election years 1920, 1923, 1926 and 1937 as anchors.
accepted.sec: Elections and ministries under dyarchy  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who was the first Premier of the Madras Presidency under the Justice Party ministry?
accepted.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar was the first Premier, serving from 17 December 1920 until July 1921 because of ill health.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from the longer-serving successor.
accepted.sec: Elections and ministries under dyarchy  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which Justice Party Premier served from 1921 to 1926 and headed two ministries?
accepted.x: Panagal Raja, also known as P. Ramarayaningar, served as Premier from 1921 to 1926 and headed two ministries.
accepted.tq: Associate the tenure with the correct premier rather than the party founder.
accepted.sec: Elections and ministries under dyarchy  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the tenure of a Justice Party Premier?
accepted.x: B. Munuswamy Naidu served from 1930 to 1932. Bobbili Raja served from 1932 to 1937, Panagal Raja from 1921 to 1926, and Subbarayalu Reddiar from December 1920 to July 1921.
accepted.tq: Use tenure overlap and sequence to eliminate swapped office-holders.
accepted.sec: Elections and ministries under dyarchy  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who acted as Premier of Madras from April to August 1936 during the tenure of the Bobbili Raja ministry?
accepted.x: P.T. Rajan acted as Premier from April to August 1936 during the period of the Bobbili Raja ministry.
accepted.tq: Test the brief acting tenure hidden within a longer ministry.
accepted.sec: Elections and ministries under dyarchy  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The independent P. Subbarayan ministry of 1926–1930 functioned with the support of the:
accepted.x: P. Subbarayan headed an independent ministry from 1926 to 1930 with the support of the Justice Party.
accepted.tq: Identify the supporting party rather than the formal label of the ministry.
accepted.sec: Elections and ministries under dyarchy  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Panagal Raja was associated with which combination of offices and facts?
1. President of the Justice Party
2. Premier from 1921 to 1926
3. Association with Andhra University in 1926
4. Death on 16 December 1928
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Panagal Raja was party president, served as Premier from 1921 to 1926, was associated with Andhra University in 1926 and died on 16 December 1928.
accepted.tq: Verify a personality through office, institutional association and date.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of the party - office held  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes K.V. Reddy Naidu in relation to the Justice Party?
o: He was the first Premier in 1920 and resigned due to ill health.
He acted as Premier from April to August 1936.
He founded the South Indian Liberal Federation in 1916.
He was a minister in the first ministry and became Premier in 1937.
accepted.x: Kurma Venkata Reddy Naidu of Eluru was a minister in the first ministry in 1920 and became Premier in 1937.
accepted.tq: Match the leader with the two offices held at different times.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of the party - office held  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Bobbili Raja, also known as Ramakrishna Ranga Rao, was the:
accepted.x: Ramakrishna Ranga Rao was the 13th Raja of Bobbili and served as Premier from 1932 to 1937. He was also a delegate to the Second Round Table Conference.
accepted.tq: Use the hereditary title to identify the correct political personality.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of the party - office held  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who moved the separate Andhra resolution in 1922, which was later withdrawn at A.P. Patro’s urging?
accepted.x: M. Suryanarayana moved the separate Andhra resolution in 1922, and it was withdrawn at the urging of A.P. Patro.
accepted.tq: Separate the mover of a resolution from the person who urged its withdrawal.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of the party - office held  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: K.V. Reddy Naidu — editor of Justice
accepted.x: Munukuru Rama Rao was associated with organising the party in Krishna. A.P. Patro was Education Minister, while M. Suryanarayana was associated with Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Start with the regional and office associations that are least interchangeable.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of the party - office held  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the language of the newspaper and its editor?
o: Andhra Prakasika — Tamil; P. Thyagaraya Chetty
accepted.x: Justice was an English newspaper edited by T.M. Nair. Dravidian was in Tamil and Andhra Prakasika was in Telugu.
accepted.tq: Match both language and editor, not merely the newspaper name.
accepted.sec: Party newspapers - language and editor  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a major reason for the decline of the Justice Party?
o: Its refusal to participate in provincial elections
Its opposition to both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement
Its strong mass base among all sections in Andhra
Its merger with the Congress before 1920
accepted.x: The party suffered from Andhra–Tamil rivalry, lacked a mass base in Andhra and opposed both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement.
accepted.tq: Select the historically stated cause while rejecting absolute organisational claims.
accepted.sec: Decline and later transformation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which development followed the Justice Party’s defeat in 1937?
o: It merged with the Independent Labour Party.
Periyar became dominant and the political stream later ran into the Dravidar Kazhagam.
It formed the first ministry under Rajaji.
C.R. Das became its leader and renamed it the Swaraj Party.
accepted.x: After the 1937 defeat, Periyar became dominant, and the stream later developed into the Dravidar Kazhagam.
accepted.tq: Test the later transformation of an organisation after electoral decline.
accepted.sec: Decline and later transformation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who criticised the neglect of the poor and Harijans within the Justice Party?
accepted.x: C. Natesa Mudaliar criticised the Justice Party for neglecting the poor and Harijans.
accepted.tq: Distinguish internal criticism from external political opposition.
accepted.sec: Decline and later transformation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to deaths of Justice Party leaders is correctly matched?
accepted.x: P. Thyagaraya Chetty died on 25 April 1925, while Panagal Raja died on 16 December 1928.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two close organisational personalities and dates.
accepted.sec: Decline and later transformation  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The colonial government used the Justice Party primarily as a counter to:
o: the Swadeshi movement and the Khilafat movement
the Andhra University movement and the Dalit movement
the Round Table Conferences and the Simon Commission
accepted.x: The government used the Justice Party against the Home Rule movement and Gandhi’s movements.
accepted.tq: Identify the political movements against which an organisation was deployed.
accepted.sec: Relations with Congress and the Swaraj Party  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who moved the no-confidence motion against Panagal Raja on 26 November 1923?
accepted.x: C.R. Reddy moved the no-confidence motion against Panagal Raja on 26 November 1923.
accepted.tq: Match the parliamentary action with its mover and date.
accepted.sec: Relations with Congress and the Swaraj Party  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In 1926, C.V.S. Narasimha Raju declined to form a ministry.
2. Panagal Raja was also unable to form a ministry in that situation.
3. The Swaraj Party was formed within the Congress in 1923.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. In 1926, C.V.S. Narasimha Raju declined to form a ministry and Panagal Raja could not form one either; the Swaraj Party had been formed within the Congress in 1923.
accepted.tq: Combine the 1926 ministry episode with the origin and date of the Swaraj Party.
accepted.sec: Relations with Congress and the Swaraj Party  [GROUP-II]
